2. The pre-emptee purchaser being the petitioner herein has filed an application before this court supported by an affidavit annexing the certified copy of the khatian of the disputed holding. The relevant Khatian No. 1814 is in mouza Sylhet Municipality J.L. No. 91. Admittedly the pre-empted suit land consisting of plot Nos. 7355 and 7356 are recorded in the aforesaid khatian. It appears from the said khatian that the superior interest over the disputed plots of land was held by the Dy Commissioner of Sylhet on behalf of the Govt. and that it was leased in the name of one Bipin Chandra Dey. This khatian was prepared after the enforcement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and prior to the filing of the pre-emption case. Both the pre-emptor and pre-emptee are purchasers either from Bipin Chandra Dey or their heirs. But, in any event, the superior interest is held by the Government. 

 3. Under the provision of sub-section (2) of section 85 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act it is provided that right to pre-empt under section 24 of the act shall not apply to any non-agricultural land held by a tenant under the Govt. prior to the enforcement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In such circumstances no pre-emption case with regard the disputed suit laud can lie under section 24 read with sub-section (2) of section 85 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. In this connection it may be referred that it is stated by the learned advocate for the petitioner that in the town of Sylhet all lands were rent-free under the Government and there was no private superior landlord as such as prevailing in other parts of the country. Be that as it may in view of the clear provision of sub-section (2) of section 85 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act and in view of the Khatian of the disputed land showing the superior interest of the Government, the application for pre-emption under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act is not maintainable in law.
